newsitem.title: INDIA: Court orders arrest of Indian politician.
newsitem.headline: Court orders arrest of Indian politician.

text.p: A special investigative court on Friday issued arrest warrants against the chief minister of India's eastern state of Bihar and three other politicians in connection with a $280 million corruption scandal.

The special court set up by the federal Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) ordered the arrests of Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav, Animal Husbandry Minister Bhola Ram Toofani, Labour Minister Vidya Sagar Nishad and former central minister Chandradeo Prasad Verma.
The special court ordered that the four politicians be produced before it on August 6, court officials said. No further details were immediately available.
The arrest warrants were issued a day after the Patna High Court rejected a plea by Yadav for anticipatory bail, which is allowed under Indian law to people who wish to avoid possible arrest.
Yadav says he is innocent in the scandal and has refused to resign from his post. His lawyers have said they will appeal any detention before India's Supreme Court.

The arrest order was issued even as senior leaders of India's ruling United Front coalition were meeting in the capital New Delhi to discuss whether or not to include Yadav's breakaway faction in the alliance.
